name: ArisInfra Solutions Ltd
title: ArisInfra Solutions Ltd - 544419 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Partner capacity rose 9.1 to 11.7 mn MT with no capex and utilisation only 42-45%, while NWC fell to 54 days and deposits fell INR 13 cr; growth guidance held at 30-35% for FY28.

summary.headline: ArisInfra Q2 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR 308 crore and EBITDA margin expanded to 11.6%, with PAT up 50% to INR 23 crore.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 308 crore (+28% YoY, +6% QoQ), with EBITDA up 58% YoY to INR 36 crore and PAT up 50% to INR 23 crore. H1 FY27 revenue grew 32% to INR 599 crore and PAT more than doubled to INR 43 crore. Contract manufacturing and DaaS reached 66% of Q2 revenue versus 53% a year earlier. Management reiterated FY30 guidance of about INR 3,000 crore revenue and 12-13% EBITDA margin, and said growth will not need new equity.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR 20 crore in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR 162 crore (LT INR 149 crore, ST INR 12 crore)
financial_highlights.change: down from about INR 200 crore last quarter

segments.name: Contract manufacturing
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue INR 329 crore (+72% YoY, 55% of H1 revenue); partner capacity raised from 9.1 to about 11.7 million tons across aggregates, RMC, concrete and asphalt, with 11 partners across four markets. Management says no single partner exceeds a quarter of capacity.

segments.name: DaaS (Developer as a Service)
segments.commentary: GDV under execution rose to INR 2,750 crore-plus from INR 1,839 crore at end-Q1 and INR 1,267 crore at end-FY26, across 15 active projects (up from 10). Fees are 10-14% of GDV, with EBITDA margin about 59% on DaaS per management.

segments.name: Materials (B2B supply)
segments.commentary: Management is moving away from lower-value trading in select categories and redirecting repeat demand to contract-manufactured supply. No segment-level revenue figure was given for this quarter.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue growth guided at 35-40%; H1 growth of 32% means H2 must carry the balance (management said 'around 30-35%' YoY for later years).
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 11.5-12%; 12-13% by FY30.

FY30 revenue target of about INR 3,000 crore, with contract manufacturing going from about INR 500 crore to about INR 2,000 crore and DaaS revenue about 10% of the total; FY30 excludes inorganic growth.
Growth funding of about INR 290-300 crore to be met through working capital lines and internal accruals; no new equity raise planned.
Steady-state net working capital target of 60-70 days as the business grows; no further investment planned in the next financial year beyond the INR 60 crore already planned this year.
DaaS GDV needed to reach about INR 300 crore revenue is roughly INR 6,000 crore; management says pick-and-choose opportunity exists until DaaS turnover reaches about INR 1,000 crore.
capex_capacity: Partner manufacturing capacity raised from 9.1 million tons (end-March) to about 11.7 million tons by Q2, with about 8 new plants added in Q2 (about 15 plants in total at 30 June), mostly RMC and asphalt.
Utilisation is about 42-45%, giving at least 6-9 months of headroom before new capacity is needed, per management.
Capacity is secured through partner arrangements without own plant capex; vendor deposits were reduced by about INR 13 crore while capacity grew.
Inventory value of secured capacity is more than INR 1,400-1,500 crore, per management.

About INR 114 crore of fixed deposits are pledged as security against own borrowings, bank guarantees and a corporate guarantee to a third party; management says this is a step toward non-fund-based support for partners.
demand_pricing: Top-10 customer contribution is about 45-47%, spread across multiple projects and regions; no single customer is said to be concentrated.
Contract manufacturing long-term demand contracts include an INR 800 crore deal with a large EPC contractor and a INR 500-600 crore contract over five years.

Pricing in contract manufacturing is dynamic and not a fixed percentage; it depends on customer size, recurring demand and credit period. Raw-material price changes are passed through almost in real time.
DaaS portfolio is about 60-65% plotted development and 30% apartments, 20% commercial; management says there is no direct competitor offering all three M's (money, material, management).
Debtors are about 33-34% of revenue, with receivable days around 150 per management.

qa_highlights.question: How should capacity additions and utilisation be read, given 2.6 million tons added this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management corrected the Q1 plant count (10 was partner entities; about 15 plants at 30 June) and said capacity is 9.1 to 11.7 million tons, with utilisation at 42-45%. It gives no capacity guidance and says capacity will run ahead of demand.

qa_highlights.question: What is the DaaS revenue benchmark and recognition method?
qa_highlights.answer: Gross fees are 10-14% of GDV. Revenue is recognised across a fixed time-based fee, a share of sales achieved and construction milestones. Projects run 6 to 30 months.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the path to 12-13% EBITDA margin by FY30?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to the mix shift toward contract manufacturing and DaaS, which together are expected to reach close to 75% of sales, plus operating leverage and geographic expansion.

qa_highlights.question: Are working capital and investment needs changing?
qa_highlights.answer: Net working capital is at 54 days and should settle at 60-70 days at steady state. The only planned investment this year is INR 60 crore, with none planned next year; the main use of cash is material purchase funding.

qa_highlights.question: Is the margin sustainable, and what is the DaaS competitive position?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to 11.5-12% for FY27 and 12-13% by FY30 and said the margin is sustainable. It sees no direct DaaS competitor, as its end-to-end service consolidates outsourced real estate functions.

qa_highlights.question: How exposed is the business in a real estate downturn?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 60-65% of the DaaS portfolio is plotted development, which holds up better in a slowdown. Projects are 10-14 storey towers with 13-18 month cycles, and no five-year-plus projects are taken.

qa_highlights.question: Why did vendor deposits fall, and is contingent liability a concern?
qa_highlights.answer: Deposits fell from about INR 200 crore to INR 162 crore. Management said the INR 114 crore fixed-deposit pledge lets partners borrow from their banks against Aris's FDs, so cash stays on balance sheet and earns interest.

risks_watch: Working capital and cash conversion: management called it the key uncertainty; receivable days are about 150 and debtors about 33-34% of revenue.
Revenue growth must accelerate in H2 to reach the 35-40% FY27 guide after 32% in H1.
DaaS execution: GDV needs to rise from INR 2,750 crore to about INR 6,000 crore for INR 300 crore revenue, with skilled supervisory staffing needed.
Contingent liability from the INR 114 crore fixed deposit pledge and the corporate guarantee given to a third party.
Real estate cycle exposure: 50-55% of DaaS portfolio is apartments and commercial, which management concedes would be impacted in a downturn.
Inflation and supply-chain pressure: management said raw-material cost changes pass through in near real time, but no quantified margin sensitivity was given.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth, margins and cash conversion, with specific numbers offered on capacity, working capital and DaaS. Evasive or non-committal on capacity additions and on the drivers of margin beyond mix, and it said it gives no absolute capacity guidance.
key_quotes: Contract Manufacturing and DaaS together contribute 66% of our revenue in Q2 FY27 compared with 53% in Q2 FY26.
So, we do not invest, any capital on DaaS.
Our capacity increase will always run before demand, and we want to be prepared to actually cater demand.
It is a pure service fees that comes.

adds.what: Partner manufacturing capacity raised from 9.1 to about 11.7 million tons, with about 8 new plants added in Q2 (about 15 plants total), mostly RMC and asphalt;

growth.why: FY27 revenue guided at 35-40% (midpoint 37.5%) with H1 at +32%, so H2 must accelerate; delivery backed by partner capacity up from 9.1 to 11.7 Mt with 43-45% utilisation, a DaaS GDV pipeline of INR 2,750 crore-plus, and two named long-term contracts (INR 800 crore and INR 500-600 crore), but no quantified H2 order book bridge.
